dedupe_keys.name: critical infrastructure interdependency metrics for canada from input output tables 1997 2023

description: This dataset accompanies a paper that measures how interdependencies among Canada's critical infrastructure sectors have changed over about 25 years, using statistical analysis of national economic accounts, and finds that interdependency, and so risk, has increased significantly. It includes the finished research paper as a PDF, raw Statistics Canada symmetric input-output tables for many years from 1997 to 2021 and US Bureau of Economic Analysis files, modelled intermediate-demand tables, a spreadsheet modelling GDP against critical infrastructure from 1997 to 2023, supply-use summaries for 2017 to 2022 and figures. The author outlines uses of the metrics in policy development, regulation, risk management, exercising and modelling. It was deposited by Tyson Macaulay on Borealis and released in March 2024, with files downloadable in XLS, XLSX and tab-separated formats under CC0 1.0. Caveats: interdependency is inferred from monetary transactions in input-output tables, not physical or service links, and the data are national aggregates. It supports interdependency and cascading failure analysis and economic resilience modelling; a related record is the Dutch critical infrastructure interdependency matrix.
name: Critical infrastructure interdependency metrics for Canada from input-output tables (1997-2023)
notes: Reference: Macaulay, T. (2024). Critical Infrastructure Interdependency. Borealis. doi:10.5683/SP3/Y2CMPZ
